source.title: Localizing Model Behavior with Path Patching
source.authors: Nicholas Goldowsky-Dill; C. Macleod; L. Sato; Aryaman Arora

record.tranche_reason: Uses path patching to causally test which paths mediate induction-like next-token prediction in a trained attention-only transformer. This is a different method from the original training-dynamics and head-identification analyses.
record.gate_note: The induction-section path-patching results are included. The paper's cited findings from other work and its GPT-2 number-completion experiments concern a different behavior and are not rows.
record.test_reason: Path patching, a different method from the originals, quantifies how much of a 2-layer attention-only model's induction behaviour the minimal previous-token-head to induction-head account explains. It then refines that account. This bears directly on V1's mechanism claim. The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find prefix matching and copying relatively separate, with head 1.5 copying with and without prefix matching. The minimal account captures little; modest added paths give a better but approximate explanation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses path patching on held-out token-level loss to iteratively test and refine path-mediation hypotheses in one trained model; it does not study when induction heads emerge during training.
record.method_sensitivity: Results change with which paths are retained and with dataset subset; longer query/key context improves the account, and adding paths for repeated-token parroting raises the reported proportion explained.
record.problems: The induction evidence is from one 2-layer attention-only model and a specified held-out OpenWebText distribution. Results are approximate path-sufficiency measures, not proof of a complete mechanism; no uncertainty estimates are reported.
record.rows_left_out: None of the reported induction path-patching results were left out. GPT-2 number-completion experiments were omitted because they study a different behavior.

untested.parts: How the heads form during training; whether the composition result holds in other models or sizes. Only one 2-layer attention-only shortformer model is studied.
No training dynamics, phase change or loss bump.
No cross-family, cross-run or cross-architecture comparison. The GPT-2 experiments concern number completion, not induction.
Training data and setup are not varied.

missing.what: Positional-Q + Positional-K combined hypothesis, 52.5% proportion explained
Attention-pattern identification of head 0.0 as previous-token head and heads 1.5/1.6 as induction heads; head 0.6 attends to multiple recent tokens

record.verdict_notes: The 0.702 baseline loss difference (R1) and the 0.432 full-dataset ATE (R13) appear to come from different dataset definitions. The paper does not reconcile them. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The GPT-2 sections were rightly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: Tests path contributions to induction-like next-token prediction in one trained 2-layer attention-only model; does not test how the heads formed during training or whether the result generalizes to other models.
No training-time formation measurements, in-context-learning time course, or training-loss curve.
No large-transformer or broad in-context-learning loss-by-token-index test.
No cross-family, size, run, architecture, or modality comparison.
Uses dataset subsets to distinguish induction from repeats, but does not vary training data or setup to test head formation or persistence of in-context learning.
Does not test few-shot task learning or compare its mechanisms with induction heads.
Does not measure formation over training or test whether formation consists of multiple transitions.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Path-patch all paths through induction heads 1.5 and 1.6 as unimportant; measure mean per-token absolute loss difference.

conditions.value: first 300 tokens of 100K held-out OpenWebText examples
all paths through heads 1.5 and 1.6 patched

rows.measure: mean per-token absolute loss difference from original model
rows.note: The paper describes this as the baseline hypothesis that the induction heads do not matter.
rows.check: This is the total effect of patching heads 1.5/1.6 (0.702 loss difference), used as the 0% reference. It shows the heads matter but has no comparison, so it is not a partial result. It also differs from Table 4's full-dataset ATE of 0.432, which the paper does not explain.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Test Direct-V: retain the induction-head value-input path from token j via the skip connection and patch paths through layer-0 heads.

conditions.value: first 300 tokens of 100K held-out OpenWebText examples

rows.baseline: 0% means as inaccurate as the hypothesis that induction heads do not matter; 100% means equal loss to the original on every example
rows.note: The direct-value path alone leaves a substantial unexplained effect.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Test Direct-Q: retain the induction-head query-input path from token i via the skip connection and patch paths through layer-0 heads.

conditions.value: first 300 tokens of 100K held-out OpenWebText examples

rows.baseline: 0% means as inaccurate as the hypothesis that induction heads do not matter; 100% means equal loss to the original on every example
rows.note: The direct-query path alone leaves a substantial unexplained effect.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Test PTH-K: retain paths from the previous-token head to the induction-head key, while allowing the previous-token head to use the current or an earlier token.

conditions.value: first 300 tokens of 100K held-out OpenWebText examples

rows.baseline: 0% means as inaccurate as the hypothesis that induction heads do not matter; 100% means equal loss to the original on every example
rows.note: The paper reports 53.3% here; Table 2 gives 53.5% for PTH-K.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Test All-Initial: retain the union of the Direct-V, Direct-Q, and PTH-K paths; patch other paths.

conditions.value: first 300 tokens of 100K held-out OpenWebText examples

rows.baseline: 0% means as inaccurate as the hypothesis that induction heads do not matter; 100% means equal loss to the original on every example
rows.note: The paper states that this sparse initial hypothesis fails to capture most of the behavior.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Test Positional-V by adding paths from token j through each layer-0 head to the induction-head value input.

conditions.value: first 300 tokens of 100K held-out OpenWebText examples

rows.baseline: 0% means as inaccurate as the hypothesis that induction heads do not matter; 100% means equal loss to the original on every example
rows.note: Adding paths through layer-0 heads substantially improves the value-path hypothesis.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Test Positional-Q by adding paths from token i through each layer-0 head to the induction-head query input.

conditions.value: first 300 tokens of 100K held-out OpenWebText examples

rows.baseline: 0% means as inaccurate as the hypothesis that induction heads do not matter; 100% means equal loss to the original on every example
rows.note: Adding paths through layer-0 heads improves the query-path hypothesis.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Test Positional-K by restricting the PTH-to-key paths to the token at j−1 through layer-0 heads.

conditions.value: first 300 tokens of 100K held-out OpenWebText examples

rows.baseline: 0% means as inaccurate as the hypothesis that induction heads do not matter; 100% means equal loss to the original on every example
rows.note: The paper says this was not a significant improvement over PTH-K.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Test All-Positional: combine the positional versions of the value, query, and key hypotheses and patch other paths.

conditions.value: first 300 tokens of 100K held-out OpenWebText examples

rows.baseline: 0% means as inaccurate as the hypothesis that induction heads do not matter; 100% means equal loss to the original on every example
rows.note: The expanded positional hypothesis still leaves a substantial unexplained effect.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Test PTH-K again as the comparison in the positional-hypothesis results.

conditions.value: first 300 tokens of 100K held-out OpenWebText examples

rows.check: Duplicates R4: the same PTH-K hypothesis reprinted in Table 2 as 53.5% versus 53.3% in Table 1. It should be merged with R4, noting the discrepancy.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Apply All-Long path patching and measure average unexplained effect on the full dataset.
rows.note: The table reports the AUE and its ATE baseline.
rows.check: AUE 0.244 / ATE 0.432 gives about 43.5% explained. That is lower than the 55.2% All-Long figure in Table 3, and the paper does not reconcile the two datasets.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Apply All-Long path patching and measure average unexplained effect on the induction subset.
rows.note: The authors define the induction subset by reference to prior work.
rows.check: On the induction subset, All-Long explains about 76% (1 − 0.219/0.907). That is near-full for the induction behaviour V1 names, so 'partial' understates it.

source_check.correct: state=partial. All-Long has AUE 0.219 against ATE 0.907 on the induction subset, giving approximately 75.9% explained and 24.1% unexplained. The text does not characterize this as full or nearly full recovery.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.5; Table 4, Induction subset; Section 2.5, proportion-explained formula.
source_check.problem: The verdict fix upgrades substantial but incomplete explanation to observed without support for the near-full interpretation.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Apply All-Long path patching and measure average unexplained effect on the uncommon-repeats subset.

conditions.value: repeats subset: previously occurring tokens outside the 200 most common validation-set tokens

rows.note: The paper describes performance as worse on this subset and interprets the gap as evidence of a distinct parroting behavior.
rows.check: About 46% explained on the repeats subset. This measures copying without prefix matching (parroting), not [A][B]…[A]→[B]. It bears on V1 only as evidence that the heads do more than induction.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V1 from this row alone. The repeats subset selects previously occurring uncommon tokens, whether or not induction is helpful; it does not isolate prefix matching. AUE=0.777; ATE=1.444.
source_check.locator_found: Section 3.5; Table 4, Repeats subset; Appendix C.
source_check.problem: Incomplete explanation of repeated-token copying does not by itself measure incomplete V1 induction; the subset also includes induction cases.

rows.subject: 2-layer attention-only autoregressive transformer
rows.operation_detail: Add paths from token j through layer-0 attention or skip connections to head 1.5's key input, forming All-Final.
rows.baseline: 0% means as inaccurate as the hypothesis that induction heads do not matter; 100% means equal loss to the original on every example
rows.note: The authors report an increase of 18.3% over All-Long and 45.3% over All-Initial.

relationships.condition: Induction subset, 2-layer attention-only model, All-Long paths (previous-token/recent-token head to induction-head key, plus query and value paths)
relationships.reason: PTH-to-key composition paths plus query and value paths explain about 76% of induction-subset loss effect (R14). PTH-K alone explains 53% (R4).
relationships.display_finding: Previous-token-to-key composition with additional query and value paths explained about 76% of the induction-subset loss effect; previous-token-to-key composition alone explained 53% on the broader evaluation distribution.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: Induction subset, 2-layer attention-only model, All-Long paths (previous-token/recent-token head to induction-head key, plus query and value paths)
source_check.reason: R14 leaves approximately 24.1% unexplained even after adding layer-0 paths and longer context beyond the minimal previous-token composition. R4 is a partial result on the broader evaluation distribution, not the induction subset. These results support a contribution while qualifying the simple mechanism account.

relationships.condition: Full held-out OpenWebText distribution; the minimal two-head account
relationships.reason: The minimal All-Initial account explains 28.2% (R5). Gains require extra layer-0 head paths, a 3-token recent-tokens context, and head 1.5 'parroting' (R6-R9, R11-R13, R15). All-Final reaches only 73.5% (R16).
relationships.display_finding: The minimal circuit explained 28.2% of the loss effect, rising to 73.5% after adding layer-0 paths, three-token context, and head 1.5 parroting behavior.

source_check.condition: Full held-out OpenWebText distribution; the minimal two-head account
source_check.reason: R5 explains only 28.2%; added layer-0 and longer-context paths improve the approximation, and R16 reaches 73.5%. R15 supplies context about additional copying behavior but does not independently isolate V1 induction.

tranche.reason: Path patching quantitatively tests and refines the induction mechanism using a different intervention method in a trained attention-only model.

source_check.notes: The paper announces open-source code. Table 1 and Table 2 differ on PTH-K (53.3% versus 53.5%); Table 4 full-dataset values imply approximately 43.5% explained, unlike Table 3's 55.2%, without an explicit reconciliation. AUE measures distribution-specific sufficiency, not completeness.

statements.correction: Table 1: PTH-K=53.3% on the Section 3.1 evaluation distribution. All-Long includes added layer-0 paths and longer query/key context with K=3. Table 4 induction subset: AUE=0.219; ATE=0.907; derived proportion explained approximately 75.9%.
statements.problem: The 53.3% and approximately 76% figures are correct, but the latter is not obtained merely by adding query and value paths to PTH-K. It uses the broader All-Long hypothesis and a different evaluation subset.

statements.correction: Comparable component refinements: Direct-V 64.1% to Positional-V 86.2%; Direct-Q 48.7% to Positional-Q 72.6%; Positional-Q plus Positional-K 52.5% to Long-QK 59.5%. Combined refinements: All-Initial 28.2%; All-Positional 48.6%; All-Long 55.2%; All-Final 73.5%.
statements.problem: The values are correct, but the listed hypotheses are not a successive sequence of added paths: Positional-V and Positional-Q test different inputs, and Long-QK jointly tests query and key paths.

statements.correction: Abstract and introduction: an open-source framework is provided. All-Long includes additional layer-0 paths and longer query/key context with K=3. Induction subset: AUE=0.219; ATE=0.907; derived proportion explained approximately 75.9%. One model is used for the induction investigation.
statements.problem: The no-code characterization contradicts the abstract and introduction. The approximately 76% result also requires the expanded All-Long paths, rather than merely adding query and value paths to PTH-K. The paper alone cannot establish the claimed uniqueness among papers.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Refined path hypotheses in the tested 2-layer attention-only model
reader_labels.reason: Path-patching results show substantial mediation by induction-head paths, with the refined All-Final account explaining 73.5% of the behavior (R6-R7, R11-R16).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Initial and less-complete path hypotheses, and the repeats subset
reader_labels.reason: Initial hypotheses explain only 28.2% jointly, and the All-Long account has greater unexplained effect on repeats than on the induction subset; the authors identify additional paths and parroting beyond the minimal account (R1-R5, R8-R10, R15).
